title: tenanted-fallback-orchestrator-and-lease-snapback-hotfix
author: Evan Brooks
release_notes: Fixes a rare tenant-lease desync during regional failover causing prolonged soft-degradation; reduces SLO violation bursts and restores normal prioritization without full-scale circuit reopen.
description: Context: We observed intermittent multi-tenant SLO spikes during regional failover windows where some tenants remained in a degraded path for minutes after capacity recovered. Motivation: Reduce blast radius and avoid full circuit reopen for tenants that should have snapback eligibility. Root cause: A subtle race between the tenant lease refresh path and the fallback orchestrator: when a regional health event triggers tenant-level fallback, the lease state machine could remain in a stale 'snoozed' lease if the recovery probe returned between steps, preventing the normal snapback timer from running. This caused tenants to be deprioritized longer than necessary and forced more aggressive global mitigation. Design summary: Introduce a short-lived epoch token tied to a tenancy lease refresh and make the fallback decision path validate epoch currency before persisting long-duration snooze state. Add a conservative snapback accelerator that allows fast re-evaluation of tenants that meet latency and error-rate thresholds within a recovery window. Implementation details: 1) core/orchestrator/fallback_manager.go: add epoch token checks to persistSnooze and a new in-memory fast-snap queue for candidates eligible for accelerated re-eval. 2) core/orchestrator/lease_manager.go: emit lease-epoch on successful refresh and surface it to the fallback manager via a non-blocking channel. 3) core/slo/enforcer.go: add a soft-credit accounting adjustment so fast-snap candidates are temporarily favored for small token allotments to prevent starvation. 4) k8s CRD update deploy/k8s/tenanted-lease-crd.yaml: add optional field fastSnapWindow with default 30s so operators can tweak. 5) tests: refine pkg/routing/regional_failover_test.go to simulate interleaved lease refresh and recovery probe timing; add a new test that reproduces the original desync. 6) docs/ops/fallback-runbook.md: document the safe rollback and toggles. Non-blocking invariants: epoch tokens are ephemeral and do not change existing lease semantics; snapshot persistence is guarded by a TTL to avoid stale state. Testing: added unit tests that cover epoch mismatches, integration test that replays a production-like failover trace (reused recorded trace from SUP-9081). Load test run in benchmark lab reproduced the condition previously causing 2.5x SLO burst; after the change the burst reduced by >90% in local sim. CI: initial integration run hit a flaky integration test (routing/probe flake) unrelated to the hotfix; reran and all checks passed. Rollout plan: merge to main, staged rollout via feature toggle fast_snap_enabled=false by default; enable in dedicated Canary region for 6 hours, monitor per-tenant SLOs and circuit transitions; if stable, flip in remaining regions over 24h. Rollback plan: toggle fast_snap_enabled=false and revert the CRD fastSnapWindow to 0. Follow-ups: duration-tuning analysis and a small telemetry job to count epoch mismatches and fast-snap churn (ENG-4330). Related: links to SUP-9081 for incident traces and ENG-4321 for design doc.

review_comments: Asha Patel (2026-02-21): Nice catch on the epoch token. Two questions: 1) can a malicious tenant force epoch churn and cause extra CPU by spamming refresh? 2) please add an invariant comment near persistSnooze so future authors understand the TTL guard.

Evan Brooks (2026-02-21): Responses: 1) epoch tokens are issued only on successful lease refresh which has rate limits at the control-plane side; we added a per-tenant token cooldown check in lease_manager.go to defend against refresh storms. 2) added inline comments and a unit test for TTL guard (see commit 2c7e4a1).

Diego Ramos (2026-02-22): Integration test reproduces the timing window but I see one flake in probe harness; suggest adding a small jitter to the recovery probe in test harness to catch races. Also request adding a metrics tag fast_snap_result for observability.
Evan Brooks (2026-02-22): Added jitter in the test harness and emitted fast_snap_result metric with buckets success/skip/stale in 8f3a2b3 and updated docs to include the new metric name.
Samantha Liu (2026-02-23): Approve after patch: please ensure the CRD default stays conservative (30s) and that enabling fast_snap requires the feature toggle. Verified the RBAC changes are minimal.
Asha Patel (2026-02-24): Quick post-merge note: in a canary we saw one tenant re-eval that triggered slightly higher short-term CPU; fine for now but track with ENG-4330 telemetry job.
